payload.title: P5-09a: copy-backend: separate source/target credentials
payload.description:
## Goal
`papyrus ops content copy-backend` (Papyrus#160, released next.34) can copy between two backends that live in DIFFERENT AWS accounts, with the source opened read-only. Needed by PPY-e20cab (old backend in legacy 335163751677 to new backend in papyrus-production 712236451410). The tool is not changed beyond what is listed here.

## Gap (FACT, read on origin/develop 2026-10-09)
- src/papyrus_content/graphql_http.py: `iam_signed_graphql_headers` signs every AppSync call with ONE process-wide botocore session (`_aws_credentials()`), so source and target always use the same account.
- src/papyrus_content/backend_copy_aws.py: `resolve_location` for `stack:NAME` calls `boto3.client("cloudformation")` (ambient chain); `S3ObjectStore` builds `boto3.client("s3")` (ambient chain); `copy_object_from` is `client.copy(...)` made with the TARGET client, which needs read on the source bucket (cross-account: denied without a source bucket policy).
- src/papyrus_content/backend_copy.py `apply_plan` copies objects one at a time (53k objects would take hours).
`PapyrusGraphQLAuthoringClient` already accepts a `header_factory`, so no change to it.

## Change (smallest)
1. `backend_copy_commands.py` / CLI options: `--source-profile NAME`, `--target-profile NAME` (optional; absent = today's ambient chain, behaviour unchanged), `--expect-source-account ID`, `--expect-target-account ID` (optional; if given, `sts get-caller-identity` of that side must match or the command stops before any read or write). The plan JSON and the printed table gain `sourceAccount` and `targetAccount`.
2. `graphql_http.py`: `iam_signed_graphql_headers(endpoint, body, session=None)`; when a boto3 session is given, sign with `session.get_credentials().get_frozen_credentials()`. Default path unchanged.
3. `backend_copy_aws.py`: `resolve_location(spec, session=None)` (CloudFormation via the session); `GraphQLRowBackend` builds `PapyrusGraphQLAuthoringClient(endpoint, header_factory=...)` from its side's session; `S3ObjectStore(bucket, region, client)` gets its client from its side's session.
4. S3 transfer: `--s3-transfer auto|server-side|stream` (default auto = server-side when neither profile is given, else stream). Stream = `head_object` on the source, `get_object` stream, write with the target client preserving ContentType, CacheControl, ContentDisposition, ContentEncoding, ContentLanguage and user Metadata. ETag fidelity: if the source ETag has no `-` use a single `put_object`; if it has `-` use multipart with 8 MiB parts (all 116 multipart objects in the old media bucket are 8 MiB-part uploads, so the ETags reproduce). No object is written to local disk (disk is tight).
5. `--s3-workers N` (default 1 = today's behaviour): apply copies objects with a thread pool of N; errors are collected per key as today.
6. Source stays read-only: the source session is only used for list, head and get calls. Add a Gherkin step asserting no write method is ever called on the source client.
7. Update docs/migrations/copy-backend.md (new flags, cross-account runbook, the 8 MiB ETag note).

## Gherkin first (features_backend/copy-backend.feature)
- "each side signs AppSync requests with its own profile"
- "a stream copy preserves key, size, content type, metadata and, for 8 MiB multipart sources, the ETag"
- "without profile options the behaviour and the plan are unchanged"
- "an account mismatch against --expect-target-account stops before any read or write"
- "the source session never calls a write operation"
- "N workers copy every object exactly once and a failed key is reported, not hidden"

## Acceptance checks
- Fixture-based tests (no AWS) pass: python and the feature file, CI green.
- Read-only real dry run (no --apply) with `--source-profile legacy --target-profile papyrus-production --expect-source-account 335163751677 --expect-target-account 712236451410` against the old p.apyr.us backend and the new one prints both account ids and the per-model plan; the new backend still has 0 rows and 0 objects afterwards.
- PR into develop (never main), release, then PPY-e20cab pins the release version.

## Rollback
Code only; revert the PR. The default (no profile flags) path is unchanged.

## Needs Ryan
Review/merge of the PR. No AWS writes in this ticket.
